title: The JVP of `polynomial` has the wrong shape if the constant coefficient broadcasts `x`
description: If only the constant coefficient `a_0` of `lax.polynomial(x, coeffs)` is larger than `x` along some axis,
the tangent with respect to `x` has the shape of `x` instead of the shape of the result.
So forward mode returns a tangent of the wrong shape, reverse mode raises a `ValueError`,
and `grad` of a sum silently returns a wrong value.
expected: `lax.polynomial` broadcasts `x` and all coefficients against each other,
so the tangent should have the shape of the result, as the primal does.
For `x` of shape `(1,)` and `a_0` of shape `(3,)`, each of the three entries of `a_0 + 2 x` has slope 2 in `x`,
so the gradient of their sum is 6.
reproducer: # The linear coefficient as an array of shape (1,) and as a scalar.
# Forward mode returns a tangent of shape (1,) instead of (3,).
# Reverse mode raises, because the cotangent has the shape of the result.
# actual:  ValueError: Expected cotangent type float32[1] but got float32[3]
# actual:  ValueError: Expected cotangent type float32[1] but got float32[3]
# The gradient of the sum is silently wrong: three outputs of slope 2 give 6, not 2.
cause: where `dy_dx = polynomial(x, deriv_coeffs)` broadcasts only `x` and the coefficients of positive degree.
`a_0` drops out of the derivative and takes its shape with it,
and the tangent is never broadcast to the shape of the result.
lean: `Jax.Lax.polynomialJvp_correct` proves the rule correct if `a_0` broadcasts to the shape of `x` and the other coefficients.
The model has no rank-0 arrays, so `Jax.Lax.polynomialJvp_not_correct` uses a linear coefficient of shape `(1,)`.
JAX behaves the same for the scalar coefficient `2.0` of the upstream issue.
The domain check of `scripts/shapes.py` finds it in Lean: the tangent that the JVP rule returns
does not have the shape of the result of `polynomial`.
